title: Triangles & Parallel Lines
subtitle: Angle Sum, Exterior Angles, Transversals
bounds: Angles in tens. Every given, unknown and answer angle is a multiple of 10 from 10 to 170 degrees (an x is 10 to 90, a tens quotient). Every + and − on angles is a tens fact (180 − 70 is 18 − 7): operands and results 1-18 tens. Every × and ÷ is a times-table fact in tens: coefficients 2-9, a divisor 2-9 into 18 tens or less (6x = 180 is 18 ÷ 6), a quotient 1-9 tens. Totals: a triangle is 180, a right triangle's other two add to 90, an exterior angle equals the sum of its two remote angles (at most 170), parallel-line pairs are equal (corresponding, alternate; vertical angles of crossing lines) or add to 180 (same-side, or neighbors on a line). Isosceles base angles come from an even-tens top angle ((180 − 40) ÷ 2 is 14 ÷ 2). Similar triangles are told by two angles each; the third is 180 minus their tens sum. No 360, no half-angles, no trigonometry. Choices are plain numbers (or Equal, Add to 180, Add to 90, Yes, No); wrong choices are whatever a misreading gives (45, 98, 330), up to 999.

tiers.name: Triangle Angle Sum
tiers.description: The three angles of a triangle add to 180. Find the missing one, even in right and isosceles triangles.

tiers.name: Exterior Angles
tiers.description: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote angles, the inside angles far from it.

tiers.name: Transversal Angles
tiers.description: Parallel lines cut by a line: corresponding and alternate angles are equal, same-side angles and neighbors on a line add to 180.

tiers.name: Equal or Add to 180?
tiers.description: Decide for each pair of angles on parallel lines: equal, or adding to 180. Then tell if lines are parallel.

tiers.name: Solve for x & Similar
tiers.description: Angle equations with x in triangles and parallel lines, then similar triangles told by two angles.

USED_360.student: A triangle's angles add to 180, and so does a straight line. 360 is a full turn.
USED_360.teacher: Subtracts from 360 (a full turn) instead of 180 or 90.

FORGOT_ONE.student: Use every piece you are given. Don't leave one out.
FORGOT_ONE.teacher: Takes away only one of the given angles, or skips the +number on x.

ADDED_ANGLES.student: The missing angle is what is left of the total. Subtract, don't add.
ADDED_ANGLES.teacher: Adds the angles (or the angle and the total) instead of subtracting from the total.

USED_90.student: 90 is only for a right angle. Here the total is 180.
USED_90.teacher: Uses 90 as the total (a complement) for a triangle or for supplementary angles.

FORGOT_RIGHT.student: A right triangle already has a 90 angle. The other two add to 90.
FORGOT_RIGHT.teacher: Subtracts only the given angle from 180 and forgets the right angle.

NO_HALF.student: Two base angles share what is left. Split it in half.
NO_HALF.teacher: Gives 180 minus the top angle as one base angle, without halving it.

HALF_TOP.student: Base angles come from what is left of 180, not from half the top angle.
HALF_TOP.teacher: Halves the top angle instead of halving 180 minus the top angle.

SAME_AS_TOP.student: Only the two base angles are equal. The top angle is different.
SAME_AS_TOP.teacher: Gives the top angle as each base angle.

NO_DOUBLE.student: There are two base angles. Add both before you subtract from 180.
NO_DOUBLE.teacher: Subtracts one base angle from 180 instead of both.

SAME_AS_BASE.student: The top angle is what is left after both base angles, not a copy of one.
SAME_AS_BASE.teacher: Gives a base angle as the top angle.

SPLIT_IN_TWO.student: A triangle has three angles. Split 180 three ways, not two.
SPLIT_IN_TWO.teacher: Divides 180 by 2 instead of 3 for an equilateral triangle.

INTERIOR_FOR_EXTERIOR.student: An exterior angle makes a straight line with its inside angle. Not the same.
INTERIOR_FOR_EXTERIOR.teacher: Gives the inside angle (180 minus the exterior) where the exterior is wanted, or the reverse.

ONE_REMOTE.student: The exterior angle is both remote angles added together, not just one.
ONE_REMOTE.teacher: Gives one remote angle instead of the sum of both.

ADDED_NOT_SUB.student: The exterior angle is the SUM of the remotes. To find one remote, subtract.
ADDED_NOT_SUB.teacher: Adds the exterior and the known remote angle instead of subtracting.

EQUAL_REMOTES.student: The two remote angles need not be equal. Subtract to find the other.
EQUAL_REMOTES.teacher: Assumes the unknown remote angle equals the given one.

SAME_AS_EXT.student: The exterior angle and its inside neighbor make a straight line: 180.
SAME_AS_EXT.teacher: Gives the exterior angle itself as the inside angle next to it.

SUPP_FOR_EQUAL.student: Alternate, corresponding and vertical angles are equal. Don't subtract.
SUPP_FOR_EQUAL.teacher: Treats an equal pair as supplementary: gives 180 minus the angle.

COMP_FOR_EQUAL.student: These angles are equal. 90 minus the angle is for a corner, not this.
COMP_FOR_EQUAL.teacher: Treats an equal pair as complementary: gives 90 minus the angle (or its distance from 90).

EQUAL_FOR_SUPP.student: A pair that adds to 180 is not an equal pair.
EQUAL_FOR_SUPP.teacher: Treats a same-side (supplementary) pair as equal.

GAVE_ANGLE.student: Check what is asked: you want x, not the size of an angle.
GAVE_ANGLE.teacher: Answers with an angle's size when the question asks for x.

NO_DIVIDE.student: You stopped early. Divide by the number in front of x.
NO_DIVIDE.teacher: Gets the total for the x terms and forgets to divide by the coefficient.

MULTIPLIED_NOT_DIVIDED.student: 2x means 2 times x. To undo it, divide by 2.
MULTIPLIED_NOT_DIVIDED.teacher: Multiplies by the coefficient of x instead of dividing.

SPLIT_EVENLY.student: The angles are not all equal. Add the x parts, then divide by that.
SPLIT_EVENLY.teacher: Splits the total evenly (by the number of angles) instead of by the sum of the coefficients.

USED_180.student: Use the right total. Here the angles do not add to 180.
USED_180.teacher: Uses 180 as the total for the x terms where the total is 90 or the exterior angle.

SIGN_SLIP.student: A + number on one side becomes minus when it moves to the other side.
SIGN_SLIP.teacher: Moves a +number across the equals sign without changing its sign.

GAVE_X.student: x is not the angle. Multiply x by the number in front to get the angle.
GAVE_X.teacher: Stops at the value of x when the question asks for an angle.

OTHER_ANGLE.student: Re-read the question: it asks for the largest angle.
OTHER_ANGLE.teacher: Finds x correctly but answers with the wrong angle (not the largest).

NEEDS_SAME_LISTED.student: Find each third angle. Same three angles means similar, however they are listed.
NEEDS_SAME_LISTED.teacher: Says No because the two listed angles differ, without finding the third angles.

ONE_ANGLE_ENOUGH.student: Similar needs all three angles to match. One shared angle is not enough.
ONE_ANGLE_ENOUGH.teacher: Says Yes because the triangles share one listed angle.

ALL_TRIANGLES_ALIKE.student: Every triangle adds to 180, but similar needs the same three angles.
ALL_TRIANGLES_ALIKE.teacher: Says Yes because both triangles' angles add to 180.
